rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a recognition lecture told before the experience is an abstract claim. our-product-our-system.md places [Lecture: Start from your customer's sentence] directly AFTER [Exercise: Paint the product box]; L3 'You drew the box your product would come in' is told as recognition of what was just lived.

Harm: over-lecturing steals the closer's felt evidence. Day 1 is vindication, not a contrast-mood module, and this lecture sits after its exercise. Closest: L3 names Hohmann and 'working backwards' (practitioner terms), kept because the exercise is already done and they name what the trio did.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No cross-module sequencing in lecture bodies.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cE 'M[0-9]+|Module [0-9]' on expanded body above the maintainer fence -> 0 (planted 'M3 reads this' returns 1).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test AND the truth clause.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L1 '# Start from your customer's sentence' names the one move and the body supports it; L3 header 'Would a customer pick up the box?' names the test the slide poses (squint-approved question, header-style-distilled r12). Closest: L5 'The product box keeps the agents on course' drops the body's 'can be that reference' qualifier; the slide's own last line ('Keep the box current') bounds it and the wording is judged in slides/the-box-is-the-reference.md, so non-blocking suggestion, not a REVISE here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slide's BODY is size-bounded, not just its header (§4's sibling).
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/lectures/apt101-work-backwards.md -> 'oversized: 0 ... every slide is within limits'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A prompt inside a lecture is a trainer show-and-tell, never a room follow-along.
A new training's lectures start from the slide corpus, not from fresh prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L3 and L5 are two include lines to curriculum/slides/*.md, no fork; apt101-slide-reuse-map.md lists G1 'Work backwards' as a named gap and the second slide is an APT101 rewrite of AE101 what-packaging-is (its STATUS). Slide 1 STATUS 'Owes judging rounds' is the rule's own stated debt.

Leaves the student: validated on the craft (the box, Amazon's working backwards), and holding the box as the thing that steers agents; sets up The agent knows only what you tell it and Write the bet, which reads team/product-box.html. Closest: L9 (slide 1) 'you are not yet sure what you are building for' stays epistemic. Trace phases 8 / 8, close 8; both beats are teaching beats, none exempt.

Closest: slide 1 'If you cannot write that face, you are not yet sure what you are building for. Better to find out on cardboard than after the build.' It is conditional, names not-knowing, and frames the box as the cheap place to find out; nothing says the team did wrong.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Headers name the discipline (start from the customer's sentence; box as reference). Failure appears only as the negative case in body: 'an agent drifts' (slide 2) and 'A stale reference steers just as firmly'. No failure-word title.

Facets checked: front-run - slide 2 'Point the agents at it' is enacted next by Write the bet (apt101-d1-bet-outcome reads team/product-box.html), does not take Send it off's or Day 2's turn; the stance thread (what is your insight) is not touched. Module-to-module arc - hands to The agent knows only what you tell it. Big Idea 'do AI as a team, and stay in control' - slide 2 is control. Mood not resolved early - no Day 2 unease preempted. Closest: 'an overnight digest' names Send it off's object a few beats early (fit note, suggestion below).
